spec_features.evidence: Both tools defined in tool_specs() (harness.py), both dispatched in handle() setting signal.gave_up / signal.declared_impossible (harness.py ~131-140). declare_impossible breaks unconditionally; give_up sets stopped_reason and breaks when stop_on_abandon (agent_loop.py ~96-104).
spec_features.notes: declare_impossible always terminates; give_up terminates only when cfg.stop_on_abandon is True (default True).

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop runs to `max_turns` (default 12) unless a stopping rule fires
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_episode: 'for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop; the for/else sets stopped_reason='max_turns' when the cap is reached (agent_loop.py ~64 and ~118-119). cfg.max_turns default 12 (config.py ~line 60).
spec_features.notes: Cap is read by the loop range and enforced as the terminating bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Hard cap on agent turns. This is THE knob that bounds cost. ... a small cap is both cheap and sufficient.'

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: 'if signal.gave_up: transcript.stopped_reason = "gave_up"; if cfg.stop_on_abandon: break'. signal.gave_up set in harness.handle() for give_up. cfg.stop_on_abandon defaults True (config.py ~line 64).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and conditioned exactly on cfg.stop_on_abandon as the spec says. If False, gave_up is recorded but loop continues to max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Stop the rollout early once the agent has clearly abandoned the task, to save tokens. Set False to always run to max_turns (cleaner severity curves).'
